sections.heading: The place
paragraphs: St. Maries is a working logging town on the St. Joe River in northern Idaho. The river made the town, and the river is famous: the U.S. Forest Service calls the lower St. Joe the highest navigable river in the world. River writers add an honest footnote — “by some definitions.”
A hundred years ago, paddle-wheel steamboats carried as many as 1,000 passengers up this river. The steamboats are gone. The work isn't: tugboats still tow rafts of logs past town, down to the mills.

sections.heading: What happened here
paragraphs: In August 1910, the fire everyone here just calls the 1910 fire tore through these mountains. Firefighters died across the region, and dozens of them were brought to St. Maries and buried together at Woodlawn Cemetery, west of town.

They lie in circles around a granite marker shaped like a flame, put up by the Forest Service, and the town has kept the memorial ever since. The books don't quite agree on the count — 54 to 59 men, depending on the source — so this page prints the range instead of pretending.

bullets: Woodlawn Cemetery — the circles of firefighters' graves and the flame-shaped marker, west of town.
The riverfront — tugs towing log rafts still pass. There's no schedule; stand on the bank a while and watch the river work.
Logger's Memorial Park, downtown — a memorial naming more than 250 St. Joe loggers killed on the job.
Hughes House Museum, at Sixth and Main — a historic log house that holds the town's logging history.
The St. Joe River Scenic Byway — 47 miles upriver to Avery, through the country the log drives came down.
sections.heading: What you can see now

bullets: St. Maries has full services year-round. Local time is Pacific.
Woodlawn Cemetery is public ground in daylight. It is a working cemetery — go on the paths, and visit like a guest.
The byway is open to Avery all year. Past Avery the road isn't plowed and can be snowed shut, roughly November to May.
Hughes House hours weren't verified for this page — check before you count on it being open.
